clue.text: Richly embroidered yarns for sound high living?

indicators.note: 'sound' asks for a word that is said the same way as the phrase the next words give

parts.note: high living is living on tall storeys, the upper floors of a tall building

explanation.surface: A question about whether richly embellished yarns go with a life lived high up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tall storeys' (high floors, where high living goes on) sound the same as 'tall stories'. 'for' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Exaggerated, unlikely tales are called tall stories, and embroidering a yarn means padding it out with invented detail.

clue.text: A bit of a night prowler?

parts.note: a tom is a male cat, a creature that prowls about at night

explanation.surface: A question about part of some creature that roams in the dark.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as 'a bit of a night prowler': the definition is 'A bit', and 'a night prowler' gives A TOM. 'of' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: An atom is the tiniest particle of a substance, so it is a very small piece or a bit.

clue.text: Captain's escape order from blast of fire

indicators.note: 'from' says the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A ship's captain gets away from an explosion of flames.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'bLAST OF Fire'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tradition says a captain is the final person to leave a sinking ship, so the captain's place in the escape order is at the end.

clue.text: Advise Count

explanation.definitionFit: To tell someone what to do is to advise them, and tellers in a bank or an election are people who count.

clue.text: Withdrew weary with Communist around

indicators.note: 'around' says the word for a Communist goes round the outside of the word for weary

parts.note: a Red is a common nickname for a Communist
to weary of something is to tire of it

explanation.surface: Someone pulled out, fed up and in the company of a Communist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' wraps the Communist round the word for weary, which sits inside it just before the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To have retired is to have gone away or pulled back, a synonym of withdrew.

clue.text: Unarm ;the long day's task is done (Antony and Cleopatra")

definitions.text: Unarm ;the long day's task is done (Antony and Cleopatra")

parts.words: Unarm ;the long day's task is done (Antony and Cleopatra")
parts.note: a quotation from Shakespeare's play with one word left out: the solver supplies the name of the attendant Antony is speaking to

explanation.surface: Antony, weary after battle, tells his servant to take off his armour.
explanation.walkthrough: The full line is 'Unarm, Eros; the long day's task is done', spoken by Antony to his attendant in Act IV of Shakespeare's Antony and Cleopatra. The missing word is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In the play this Greek-named servant is Antony's armour-bearer, who later kills himself rather than kill his master.

clue.text: Playwright will brandish weapon with a point

parts.note: to brandish a weapon is to shake it threateningly
a spear is a weapon
E, for east, is one of the points of the compass

explanation.surface: A dramatist plans to wave around a sharp weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will' is a link word, though it also hints at the playwright's first name. 'with a' joins the last piece.
explanation.definitionFit: The writer of Hamlet and Macbeth is the best-known dramatist in the English language.

clue.text: Comfort for cat soon to be embroiled with lion

indicators.note: to be embroiled is to be mixed up in trouble, so these letters are mixed up together

explanation.surface: A cat is about to get into a fight with a lion and could use some reassurance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be embroiled' shuffles CATSOON with LION; 'with' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Consolation is the solace or relief offered to someone who is upset.

clue.text: A spread that's said to put a smile on our faces

definitions.text: A spread that's said to put a smile on our faces

parts.words: A spread that's said to put a smile on our faces
parts.note: a soft dairy spread for bread whose second word is what a photographer tells people to say so that they smile

explanation.surface: A sandwich filling that supposedly makes people happy.
explanation.walkthrough: Saying the second word of the answer stretches the mouth into a smile, which is why photographers ask for it.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a soft, mild, spreadable cheese made with cream, spread on bagels or crackers.

clue.text: Optimistic order to eschew mortal talk. .

explanation.definitionFit: Someone with a determined, unbeaten outlook keeps hoping, and read literally the phrase is a command to avoid the word for passing away.

clue.text: Hot gun damage?

parts.note: H is the usual abbreviation for hot, as on a tap
an arm is a weapon such as a gun, as in firearm

explanation.surface: A question about the harm done by a firearm that has been used.
explanation.definitionFit: To harm is to injure or hurt, the same as to damage.

clue.text: Spotted silent Victorian kids as expected

explanation.definitionFit: Spotted means noticed by sight, and the Victorian saying held that children should be watched but not heard.

clue.text: From Sheikh Ali fastened on to Mahdi's successor

indicators.note: 'From' says the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: An Arab leader is attached to the next ruler after a Muslim leader.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'sheiKH ALI FAstened'; 'on to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A khalifa, or caliph, is the title for a successor of a religious leader in the Islamic world, including followers of the Sudanese Mahdi.

clue.text: A shocking sort of wire in being?

parts.note: a live wire carries an electric current and gives a shock if touched

explanation.surface: A question asking whether an electrified cable is part of existence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in being' is the definition: something that is in being is in existence.
explanation.definitionFit: To be alive is to be living or existing.

clue.text: In a deep whirl allowed to reduce

indicators.note: 'In' says the word for allowed goes inside the jumbled letters of deep
a whirl spins things around, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: to let is to allow

explanation.surface: A deep whirlpool is permitted to cut something down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'whirl' scrambles 'deep', and 'In' puts the word for allowed inside that jumble near its end; 'a' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To deplete a supply is to use up a large part of it, to make it smaller.

clue.text: Classic style adopted by an old columnist

explanation.definitionFit: This plainest of the classical Greek architectural orders was a manner used by ancient builders of columns.

clue.text: Disaster whose survivors got through a two-by-two en trance

definitions.text: Disaster whose survivors got through a two-by-two en trance

parts.words: Disaster whose survivors got through a two-by-two en trance
parts.note: the Bible catastrophe that Noah's family and the animals escaped by going into the ark in pairs

explanation.surface: Survivors of a catastrophe filed in through an entrance in pairs.
explanation.walkthrough: The animals went into Noah's ark two by two, escaping the waters that covered the earth.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the great deluge of Genesis, a disaster of rising water.

clue.text: Foot's clobber?

parts.note: clobber is British slang for clothes, so this is a garment worn on a foot; to clobber is also to hit, a punch

explanation.surface: A question about what to wear on the feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clobber' is British slang for clothing and also a verb for to hit hard; the answer is both a foot garment and a punch.
explanation.definitionFit: This knitted garment is worn on the foot inside a shoe, and as a verb it means to strike with a fist.

clue.text: Wife of Osiris rises in Cotswolds

explanation.definitionFit: In Egyptian myth this goddess was married to Osiris, and the same name is used for the Thames around Oxford, which has its source in the Cotswold hills of England.

clue.text: An emptiness to shun

parts.note: an and a are both the indefinite article
a void is an empty space

explanation.surface: Someone is told to keep away from emptiness.
explanation.definitionFit: To avoid someone is to keep away from them, to shun them.

clue.text: Seamy opening a member might slip through for cover

definitions.text: Seamy opening a member might slip through for cover

parts.words: Seamy opening a member might slip through for cover
parts.note: a hole at a seam of a garment that a limb is pushed through when dressing; the member is a limb, not a club member

explanation.surface: A club member slips in through a seedy gap to hide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seamy' suggests sordid, but here it means sewn at a seam; 'member' suggests a club member, but it is a limb.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the opening in a shirt or coat where the sleeve is sewn on, through which the limb goes.

clue.text: Way the carrot was suspended made Ned glad

indicators.note: 'made' says the letters of the words that follow are formed into a new word

explanation.surface: Hanging a carrot in front of him cheered up a donkey called Ned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made' rearranges NEDGLAD; a carrot is held up in front of a donkey to lure it on.
explanation.definitionFit: A dangled carrot was hung loosely in front of the donkey as an enticement.

clue.text: Looks at raw mineral as a disfiguring feature

parts.note: to eye something is to look at it
ore is mineral rock as it is dug up, before refining

explanation.surface: Someone examines unrefined rock, which is ugly to see.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ugly that spoils a view, such as a derelict building, is called this.

clue.text: As Hunt told the Sherpas, a fine to do!

explanation.definitionFit: John Hunt led the 1953 Everest expedition, so he would have urged his porters to keep going; and a fuss or commotion is also called by this phrase.

clue.text: She follows sub privately

parts.note: a woman's name that comes after the Latin word sub to make a phrase meaning in secret

explanation.surface: A woman secretly trails a submarine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sub rosa', Latin for 'under the rose', means in confidence; 'sub' is not a submarine.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a woman's name, Latin for rose, which completes the phrase for secretly.

clue.text: In tax levies lies the core of many revolutions

indicators.note: 'In' says the letters sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Tax charges are behind many uprisings.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'tAX LEvies'; 'lies' is a link. 'Revolutions' suggests uprisings, but it means wheels turning.
explanation.definitionFit: A wheel turns round this central rod, so it is at the centre of the wheel's turning.

clue.text: Painful example of 21

parts.note: 21 across is a disfiguring feature, and read in two words it is a sore eye; this is an inflamed swelling on an eyelid

explanation.surface: An instance of an ugly feature that hurts.
explanation.walkthrough: 21 across, read as 'eye sore', describes this literally.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a painful red swelling at the edge of the eyelid, a sore on the eye.

clue.text: A bed of rock under the window

explanation.definitionFit: In geology this is a flat sheet of igneous rock between other layers, and it is also the ledge at the bottom of a window frame.

clue.text: Knockout for wild aunts who lost head

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so these letters run riot into a new order
losing a head means the first letter of the word is dropped

explanation.surface: Uncontrolled relatives who were decapitated make a stunning sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'who lost head' drops the A of AUNTS, leaving UNTS, and 'wild' rearranges those letters. 'for' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To knock someone out is to stun them, leaving them senseless.

clue.text: Stole axe, put in a frenzy to remonstrate

indicators.note: a frenzy is wild agitation, so the letters are thrown about into a new order

explanation.surface: A thief took an axe and went berserk, so someone protests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a frenzy' rearranges STOLEAXE with PUT.
explanation.definitionFit: To expostulate is to argue earnestly against something, to protest or object.

clue.text: Unlimited state of what may 22-10

explanation.definitionFit: Something without limit goes on for ever, and that is the state of whatever may continue without stopping.
